rules.rationale: Source: smiles_long lowered solubility (-11.46); logD opposes logS, so larger scaffolds should raise lipophilicity.
Source: smiles_short raised solubility (+6.89); small compact molecules are typically less lipophilic.
Heteroatom role maps from H-bond donor evidence; fewer polar atoms means weaker hydration, higher partition coefficient.
Ring role carried the strongest source transfer weight (0.758); fused hydrophobic rings favor octanol partitioning.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL solubility effects with reversed sign, assuming logD is roughly anti-correlated with logS. Fails if lipophilicity in this pool is size-saturated or driven by polar-group placement rather than bulk size.

rules.rationale: Halogen substitution raises hydrophobic surface and polarizability, a classic medicinal-chemistry driver of higher logD.
Extended aromatic pi systems provide nonpolar surface that partitions preferentially into octanol.
High heteroatom density increases hydrogen bonding and desolvation cost, suppressing measured lipophilicity.
Counter-hypothesis: low-confidence (0.224) length transfer reversed at extremes, where very long chains carry polar solubilizing groups.

skills.hypothesis: Domain-knowledge counter-hypothesis: halogen and aromatic hydrophobic surface, not molecular length, drives lipophilicity, and size effects invert at extreme lengths. Fails if halogen_high (98 candidates) is too sparse to inform the surrogate.

fixed_initial.lesson: The only quantitative source evidence comes from a different endpoint (solubility) with low per-field confidence, so sign-reversed transfer is a hypothesis, not a measurement; direct physicochemical drivers of partitioning are the safer prior.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept a sign-reversed ESOL transfer skill anchored on the reported length, heteroatom, and ring roles, and added a counter-hypothesis skill that downweights the uncertain length relation (confidence 0.224) and instead scores halogen, aromatic, and heteroatom mechanisms. Deployed the counter-hypothesis skill with moderate decaying semantic mass and a balanced UCB/EI anchor.

rules.rationale: Halogens add hydrophobic surface and polarizability, a classic driver of higher octanol-water partitioning.
Extended aromatic pi systems present nonpolar surface that partitions favorably into octanol.
High heteroatom density raises hydrogen bonding and desolvation cost, suppressing measured logD.
Ring role carried the strongest source transfer weight (0.758); fused rings add rigid hydrophobic surface.

skills.hypothesis: Merges the two development families: hydrophobic surface from halogen and aromatic content plus the high-transfer ring role, penalized by heteroatom density. Fails if halogen_high (98 candidates) is too sparse to inform the surrogate.

rules.rationale: Counter-hypothesis: polarity, not bulk size, sets lipophilicity; few heteroatoms means weak hydration.
Length transfer is low confidence (0.224, prior weight 0.040), so its reversed sign is kept but heavily downweighted.
Rotatable-bond role transferred at 0.758; flexible polar branches add hydration without nonpolar surface.
Moderate aromaticity covers a large pool (1619) with meaningful nonpolar surface but less polar substitution.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses emphasis: polarity and flexibility dominate while the uncertain size relation is nearly zeroed. Fails if bulk molecular size, not polarity, actually orders lipophilicity in this pool.

true_feedback.lesson: Across two generations of eight development seeds the two families converged (89.04/88.93 vs 85.73/89.26 mean AUC), so the earlier apparent advantage of hydrophobic-surface rules was not stable; seed-level noise exceeds the between-skill gap, and the shared ring/heteroatom terms are the most defensible components.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Because the two prior families performed indistinguishably in generation 1, I merged their overlapping mechanistic rules (halogen, aromatic, heteroatom penalty, high-transfer ring role) into one deployed skill and dropped the low-transfer extreme-length rule. The second skill is an explicit counter-hypothesis that nearly zeroes the uncertain length relation and instead emphasizes polarity and flexibility, with higher ridge and lower semantic mass to reduce variance. Deployment is frozen before held-out evaluation; no target outcomes were observed.

rules.rationale: Halogenated aromatics are the classic high-logD motif: polarizable nonpolar surface on a rigid pi scaffold.
Extended aromatic systems add nonpolar surface area that partitions preferentially into octanol; 1982 candidates give firm support.
Dense heteroatoms increase hydrogen bonding and desolvation cost, suppressing measured logD across 2661 candidates.
Few polar atoms means weak hydration; mirrors the source H-bond-donor role mapped onto heteroatom count.

skills.hypothesis: Domain prior: lipophilicity equals nonpolar surface (halogen, aromatic) minus polar hydration burden (heteroatoms). Fails if logD variance here is dominated by ionization state or scaffold size rather than atomic composition.

rules.rationale: Ring role carried the strongest transfer weight (0.758); rigid fused hydrophobic rings favor octanol partitioning.
Source length effect had lowest role confidence (0.224), so its sign-reversed bulk bonus is kept deliberately weak.
Counter-hypothesis: size benefit saturates; very long molecules typically carry solubilizing chains that lower logD.
Reverses the uncertain rotatable-bond role: heavy branching often marks polar substituents, not added hydrophobic bulk.

skills.hypothesis: Keeps only the high-weight ring transfer, damps the low-confidence length transfer, and reverses the branch role. Fails if ESOL size and flexibility effects do transfer cleanly with inverted sign to logD.

no_feedback.lesson: With no target feedback, cross-endpoint transfer stays hypothetical: low-confidence roles deserve damping, while mechanistic composition descriptors with large bin support are the safer deployment prior.
no_feedback.revision_summary: Reformatted conditions as field:value objects per schema. In the domain skill, promoted the halogen-plus-aromatic interaction to an explicit two-condition rule (a mechanistically justified halogenated-aromatic motif) and dropped the standalone halogen rule, keeping the symmetric heteroatom pair. Rebuilt the second skill as a cleaner counter-hypothesis: retain only the highest-weight ring transfer, sharply damp the low-confidence length transfer, and reverse the uncertain rotatable-bond-to-branch relation. Lowered its semantic mass and confidence accordingly, and deployed the composition-driven prior.

rules.rationale: Source: smiles_long lowered solubility (-11.46); logD opposes logS, so larger carbon scaffolds raise lipophilicity.
Source: smiles_short raised solubility (+6.89); small compact molecules expose little nonpolar surface.
Heteroatom role maps from H-bond donor evidence (weight 0.509); fewer polar atoms lowers desolvation cost.
Ring role carried the strongest source transfer weight (0.758); fused hydrophobic rings favor octanol partitioning.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size, heteroatom, and ring effects with reversed sign, treating logD as anti-correlated with logS. Fails if lipophilicity here is size-saturated or driven by polar-group placement rather than bulk hydrophobic surface.

rules.rationale: High heteroatom density raises hydrogen bonding and aqueous stabilization, so desolvation cost suppresses measured lipophilicity.
Extended pi surface with only moderate polarity yields large nonpolar contact area; chemically meaningful interaction for octanol partitioning.
Moderate halogenation raises polarizability and hydrophobic surface; halogen_mid (743) is far better supported than halogen_high (98).
Counter-hypothesis reversing the low-confidence (0.224) length transfer: extreme-length molecules often carry polar solubilizing groups, saturating or inverting the size effect.

skills.hypothesis: Domain-knowledge counter-view: polarity penalty plus aromatic and halogen hydrophobic surface drives lipophilicity, and the uncertain length relation reverses at extreme lengths. Fails if bulk molecular size dominates partitioning in this pool.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across two independent eight-seed development blocks the sign-reversed ESOL transfer skill led on mean AUC (89.59 vs 89.26 this generation; 89.04 vs 85.73 previously) and on mean final best, and it never trailed. The second-generation counterview narrowed the gap to roughly 0.3 AUC points, but the difference sits inside seed noise, so the honest read is that the source-grounded bulk and ring rules are at least as good and cheaper to justify. Eight seeds per generation cannot establish mechanism; they only justify keeping the simpler, source-grounded hypothesis in front.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Kept the proven source-transfer skill nearly frozen: raised the ring_token_high weight from 0.35 to 0.40, since the source ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758) and both generation blocks favored this skill, while leaving ridge, prior_scale, semantic mass, and the anchor blend untouched to avoid overfitting sixteen total development seeds. Rebuilt the counter-hypothesis skill around well-supported bins: dropped the sparse halogen_high anchor in favor of halogen_mid, kept the aromatic_high x hetero_mid interaction, and reformulated the very-long-length rule as an explicit size-saturation reversal of the 0.224-confidence length transfer. All conditions objects are direct field-to-value mappings drawn verbatim from the public catalog. Deployed the source-evidence-grounded transfer skill.
